subject: Proposed maintenance grace period & monthly credit allocation

Subject: Proposed maintenance grace period & monthly credit allocation

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we finalize procurement for the Q4 contract, a couple of specific asks have come up from our engineering and finance teams related to your standard uptime/latency commitments. We understand Redwood's uptime targets, but given our plan for an internal data migration in November (peak reporting), we need a temporary carve-out for scheduled maintenance windows and clarity on how monthly service credits would be calculated if incidents overlap with that migration.

Specifically, can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood will allow a one-time "maintenance grace period" in Nov where the uptime floor is adjusted to 98.0% for scheduled windows up to 8 hours total for the month without triggering standard credits;
- How service credits would be prorated if an unplanned outage happens within or adjacent to that maintenance window (we're worried about double-crediting or gaps); and
- A proposed monthly credit allocation model (e.g., flat credit vs. pro-rated by daily average spend) so our finance team can sign off.

We'd like a short counterproposal by Wednesday so procurement can circulate the amendment to legal. Happy to take a quick call if that's easier.

Best,
Lena Morris
Head of Platform Reliability, FinTechCo
Lena.morris@fintechco.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Proposed maintenance grace period & monthly credit allocation

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear notes and the migration calendar. We can be flexible here; below is an initial response to your three asks, plus a proposed counter to ensure predictable economics for both sides.

1) Maintenance grace period: Redwood is open to a one-time, customer-declared maintenance window in Nov. We'd be willing to adjust the uptime floor to 98.0% for scheduled, pre-declared maintenance totaling up to 8 hours for that month, provided windows are submitted at least 10 business days in advance and posted to the shared runbook.

2) Overlapping incidents: Our standard approach is to exclude declared maintenance from uptime calculations; however, for unplanned outages that overlap a declared window, we propose the following: credits are calculated against the eligible downtime after excluding declared maintenance duration. In other words, we will not double-credit the same elapsed minute twice, but an unplanned outage that extends beyond the declared window would be evaluated on the excess duration only. We'll add a simple example to the amendment to make this explicit.

3) Monthly credit allocation: To balance predictability, we propose a two-tier credit model for the remainder of the contract year:
- If monthly spend < $50k: flat credit equal to 10% of that month's Redwood hosting fees for each SLA band breach beyond the adjusted floor.
- If monthly spend >= $50k: prorated credit based on downtime minutes times the average per-minute cost (derived from the monthly invoice).

As a compromise, for Nov only, we propose applying the flat credit model regardless of spend to keep procurement simple. Attached is a draft amendment and a sample credit schedule for your review.

If you and procurement are comfortable with this, we'll loop in Legal and our Pricing team for redlines. I'm available for a 30-min call tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com

Folks — forwarding FinTechCo's note and my proposed counter (below). They want a one-time Nov maintenance grace period and a simplified credit model for Nov. Key asks for you:

- Priyom: is the two-tier credit model acceptable from an economics perspective? If Nov is flat-credit for all customers regardless of spend, do we need an approval for revenue impact? Please provide a rough range of expected credit exposure (conservative) for their typical monthly spend (Lena indicated ~$120k/mo current).
- Karthik: legal will need a clear clause for overlapping incidents and the exclusion language. Can you draft the redline for the maintenance carve-out and an explicit example that shows a scheduled 4-hour window and a 3-hour unplanned outage that overlaps and continues 2 hours beyond the window?

I'm proposing we accept the one-time Nov grace period with the flat-credit fallback for that month only, but we should limit frequency to once per 12-month rolling period and require advance scheduling. Thoughts please — need to get back to procurement by EOD tomorrow.

Priya — thanks for the summary. Numbers below are quick estimates; I'll formalize for Finance if you want to proceed.

Assumptions from Lena: current monthly spend ~ $120k. For Nov flat credit model (10% flat credit per band breach): worst-case single-band breach exposure = $12k. If they experience multiple qualifying breaches (unlikely, but conservative), cap at 1x monthly invoice per month as we typically do. For the prorated model (spend >= $50k) — using their $120k/month, per-minute cost ~ $120000 / (30 days * 24h * 60m) ≈ $0.055/min. So a 60-minute unplanned outage (post-exclusion) ≈ $3.30 credit.

Recommendation: Approve the one-time Nov grace period with the flat-credit approach for Nov only, and require a cap of 1x monthly invoice and a once-per-12-month customer-declared maintenance exception. That keeps exposure bounded. I'll prepare an approval note for Finance and mark expected conservative exposure at $12k for Nov.
